text:
tasha: heads up — ap-southeast1b is doing the seesaw again, a bunch of small training pods are stuck Pending while we have 20 nodes with 1 GPU idle each across racks. looks like reservation/warmpool erosion + small-gang fragmentation. anyone else seeing this?
alex: yup. started ~2h after the reservation TTL change merged. pending_gangs metric jumped.
maya: can you paste a quick kubectl output? curious whether it's a PV/affinity thing or pure binpack.
raj: here's output from one AZ: 
```
$ kubectl get pods -n ml -o wide | egrep "(Pending|ml-train)"
ml-train-aaa Pending 0/1 ap-southeast1b-node-17
ml-train-bbb Running 1/1 ap-southeast1b-node-07
ml-train-ccc Pending 0/1 ap-southeast1b-node-21
```
nodes: most show allocatable GPUs free but scheduling won't pack gangs because they request gang-size=4. small pods are blocking larger jobs; tiny pods are being spread by the scheduler's inter-pod-affinity scoring.
alex: confirmed. our binpack scoring is weighted lower than spread/zone-aware score — that's probably the reason. after the last change we bumped topologySpread to avoid NVLink-crossing but it made tiny pods scatter.
maya: cost impact note — if we keep this, larger training jobs fallback to Dedicated-hosts or wait, which increases on-demand burst and billing. rough back-of-envelope: 12h of stuck jobs -> ~2x burst in spot replacement.
raj: quick idea: temporarily reduce topologySpread weight for pods with gang scheduling >=2, and increase node binpack weight, in ap-southeast1b only. canary patch for 1 AZ.
tasha: agree. prefer AZ-only canary before org-wide. we should also tweak the descheduler to be less aggressive with tiny pods so they don't get moved mid-roll.
scheduler-bot: NOTICE: config patch request received for scheduler-config->policy:patch by raj at 2026-03-21T20:02:00Z. will validate dry-run.
alex: what about preemption thresholds? current preemptThreshold=80 makes preemption noisy and sometimes evicts small pods that then reappear elsewhere, perpetuating fragmentation. lowering to 60 might reduce churn. but that could delay important high-priority jobs.
maya: propose matrix: (A) reduce topologySpread weight from 100 -> 30 for gang>=2, (B) increase binpack weight 10 -> 40, (C) preemptThreshold 80 -> 65. apply A+B in canary, monitor 30m, if pending_gangs drops >40% then apply C. rollback plan: helm rollback scheduler-config release if pending_gangs worsens.
raj: i'll run the canary at 21:00 UTC on ap-southeast1b. will push a single AZ override via our patch script: 
```
./infractl sched-patch --az ap-southeast1b --set "topologySpreadWeight=30,binpackWeight=40" --dry-run=false
```
please don't push other scheduler changes while i'm testing.
tasha: i'll watch dashboards: Pending_gangs, Node_free_gpu_count, Preempt_events. link: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/ops/gpu-scheduler?orgId=1
autoscale-bot: Trigger: detected node-provisioning surge in ap-southeast1b at 2026-03-21T19:50:12Z — autoscaler increased pool by +4 nodes (reason: pending pods > 20m)
alex: note — autoscaler surge complicates measurement. raj, after patch wait for autoscaler to stabilize or pause autoscaler for 10m to get baseline.
raj: will pause autoscaler for 12 minutes during canary window, record results, then unpause.
maya: also log sample pod scheduling decisions (scheduler trace) for 10 affected pods so we can postmortem tie to scoring math.
tasha: ok agreed. sync: raj runs canary at 21:00 UTC, pause autoscaler, monitor for 30m, if pending_gangs drop and large-gang throughput improves we roll to rest of region with staged rollout. if not, rollback immediately. raj to post results in this thread.
raj: got it. I'll post run output + diff when done. :thumbsup:
